BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's package asserts that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted" the disclosure framework and limitation package. Nothing in our playbook or instructions supports that. These are the counterparty's drafting labels, not agreed positions, and no authority (Amelia Frost or otherwise) has been given for any of the fallbacks they rely on. I have disregarded the note and reviewed every clause on its merits. Recommend the deal team expressly reject the characterisation in the response cover email so it cannot be cited later as acquiescence.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is our own conditional fallback and cannot be conceded without prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft – none exists.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three points.** Seller's figures are 5x our positions and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250k of loss – this is the single most value-eroding limitation term in the draft.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months after Completion; plus a rider that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitation applies only to General Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" rider.** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback, and the rider is a drafting device that would silently drag Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnity claims into the general time bar (see SPA-N-014).

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside de minimis, basket and knowledge qualifiers.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** Capping title recovery at 20% means that if we do not own what we paid AUD 24m for, we recover AUD 4.8m – "administrative simplicity" is not a legitimate commercial rationale.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". No fraud carve-out anywhere in the package.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment carve-out across Cl 9.3, 12 and 20.5.** This is a non-negotiable playbook item and the current drafting purports to shield deliberate wrongdoing, which is also of doubtful enforceability.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Sch 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1] and [1.2]; require a "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter" standard against specific numbered disclosures.** Whole-data-room disclosure would gut the warranties entirely, and the Letter's own sections 2–10 show the Seller is capable of specific disclosure.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons, with any *seller* knowledge warranty tied to named seller persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete Cl 8.3 in full.** A constructive-knowledge standard ("discoverable") combined with whole-data-room disclosure means every warranty is defeated by the mere existence of the data room.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent. Disclosure Letter s.2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; Bluefen ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional consent under cl 11.2 and (b) evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft as a hard CP in Buyer's favour, with Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" plus delivery of condition-satisfaction evidence.** A 30%-of-revenue customer with an unsatisfied conditional consent is a material value risk that a "consent-on-delivery" test does not address.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter s.3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow, and executed/effective security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require payout letter, pay-direct mechanic and releases as Completion deliverables.** Completing debt-free/cash-free while AUD 3.2m of secured debt remains outstanding on a promise of a future release is inconsistent with the agreed price basis.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow excludes the DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses as "a matter for the Seller"; Disclosure Letter s.5 confirms they are not in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs either (a) a specific seller-funded line item in the funds flow or (b) treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses and deducted from price.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert specific line item with grossed-up on-costs and a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.** The bonuses are triggered by Completion and will be paid by the Company post-Completion – "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the money actually leaves the Seller's side of the funds flow.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter s.4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering failure of title to the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party IP claims, and costs of securing assignment – while preserving the cure (pay outstanding fees, obtain confirmatory assignment). AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; broaden to cover IP ownership/infringement loss arising from the Ironquay arrangement, and add a Completion deliverable of either payment receipt + confirmatory assignment or a specific escrow.** The real exposure is lack of title to deliverables, not the AUD 180k invoice itself.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter s.6: link sent to unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope unconfirmed, notification requirement undetermined; no breach admitted, no loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, and provide written updates; a specific indemnity for regulatory/notification/remediation costs arising from the incident; no assumption of breach or quantum in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; add investigation/preservation/update covenants and a specific indemnity (uncapped by general regime, sized later once facts are known).** The Seller's own Letter concedes the facts needed to assess materiality are not yet known, so neither side can call it immaterial.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter s.8: read DD-008 and DD-011 together; does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of timing, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-Completion liability; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold; request the DD-008/DD-011 terms and renewal dates, and reserve the right to treat any pre-Completion accrued or non-cancellable amount as Debt/working-capital item.** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure, but the playbook does not warrant an automatic deduction either.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3 rider ("any limitation ... applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") plus Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") plus Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities each with their own regime; no hidden override folding them into general warranty limits.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; delete the "all Claims" language and insert an express clause confirming the Cl 12 limitations apply *only* to General Warranty Claims.** This is the structural mechanism by which the Seller's 20% cap and 18-month bar would capture every other head of recovery.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter s.10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member searches, PPSR searches, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, and confirmation of no encumbrances, options or pre-emptive rights; Seller authority evidence.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as title proof; commission independent searches and require original share certificates (or cancellation), executed transfer, and encumbrance-free warranty at 100% cap.** A register maintained by the Seller's own company is a supplied internal document, not independent verification.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, AUD 25k/250k thresholds).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP warranties and indemnities remain OPEN pending separate negotiation; no assumption of unlimited liability but no acceptance of general limits either.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" assertion; respond that Tax and IP remain open and will be negotiated separately with their own cap, period (tax at least 7 years is market) and thresholds.** Nothing has been agreed and the Seller's labelling is simply the SPA-N-014 override by another name.

---

## Summary table

| ID | Issue | Seller | Rec. |
|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject → 25% / 6.0m |
| 002 | De minimis/basket | 25k / 250k deductible | Reject → 5k / 50k tipping |
| 003 | Time limit | 18m, all Claims | Reject → 24m, general only |
| 004 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Reject → 100%, 6 yrs, separate |
| 005 | Fraud | No carve-out | Reject → insert, non-waivable |
| 006 | Disclosure | Whole data room/public | Reject → specific fair disclosure |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete |
| 008 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | Reject → hard CP + condition evidence |
| 009 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Reject → pay-direct + releases at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Reject → line item + on-costs |
| 011 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Reject → broaden, keep cure |
| 012 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Reject → covenants + specific indemnity |
| 013 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Hold → assess, reserve |
| 014 | Categories | Everything into general regime | Reject → express separation |
| 015 | Title | DD-012 register | Reject → independent searches |
| 016 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject → remain open |

**Overall:** No clause in this package should be accepted as drafted. Fifteen of sixteen items require rejection or redraft; one (Sandbar) is a hold pending information. None of the Seller's positions coincide with an authorised Buyer fallback. Suggest the response mark-up lead with SPA-N-004/005/014 (structural), since fixing those also neutralises much of the damage in 001–003 and 016.

- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; broaden to cover IP ownership/infringement loss arising from the Ironquay arrangement, and add a Completion deliverable of either payment receipt + confirmatory assignment or a specific escrow.** The real exposure is lack of title to deliverables, not the AUD 180k invoice itself.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter s.6: link sent to unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope unconfirmed, notification requirement undetermined; no breach admitted, no loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, and provide written updates; a specific indemnity for regulatory/notification/remediation costs arising from the incident; no assumption of breach or quantum in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; add investigation/preservation/update covenants and a specific indemnity (uncapped by general regime, sized later once facts are known).** The Seller's own Letter concedes the facts needed to assess materiality are not yet known, so neither side can call it immaterial.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter s.8: read DD-008 and DD-011 together; does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of timing, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-Completion liability; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold; request the DD-008/DD-011 terms and renewal dates, and reserve the right to treat any pre-Completion accrued or non-cancellable amount as Debt/working-capital item.** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure, but the playbook does not warrant an automatic deduction either.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3 rider ("any limitation ... applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") plus Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") plus Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities each with their own regime; no hidden override folding them into general warranty limits.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; delete the "all Claims" language and insert an express clause confirming the Cl 12 limitations apply *only* to General Warranty Claims.** This is the structural mechanism by which the Seller's 20% cap and 18-month bar would capture every other head of recovery.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter s.10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member searches, PPSR searches, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, and confirmation of no encumbrances, options or pre-emptive rights; Seller authority evidence.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as title proof; commission independent searches and require original share certificates (or cancellation), executed transfer, and encumbrance-free warranty at 100% cap.** A register maintained by the Seller's own company is a supplied internal document, not independent verification.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, AUD 25k/250k thresholds).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP warranties and indemnities remain OPEN pending separate negotiation; no assumption of unlimited liability but no acceptance of general limits either.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" assertion; respond that Tax and IP remain open and will be negotiated separately with their own cap, period (tax at least 7 years is market) and thresholds.** Nothing has been agreed and the Seller's labelling is simply the SPA-N-014 override by another name.
